guide.title: Steakhouses in Seattle: Sixteen Rooms Inside the City Limits
guide.intro: Sixteen rooms on this page and every one of them inside the city limits, which is the whole reason this is a Seattle page and not a Puget Sound one. Seven stand in the downtown and Belltown business core: the Metropolitan Grill in the Marion Building on Second Avenue, El Gaucho in the old Union Stables on Western, the Capital Grille on Fourth, Ruth's Chris on Pine, Fogo de Chão on University, an Argentine grill on Virginia Street and the Butcher's Table up in South Lake Union. Three more sit on Capitol Hill and the lakes, with Bateau on East Union and two Daniel's Broiler rooms on the water. Five hold the north end from Ballard through Wallingford to Wedgwood, and one holds West Seattle.

sections.heading: Downtown, Belltown and South Lake Union
sections.body:
Seven rooms in the business core, and two of them are in buildings older than the trade they serve.

The Metropolitan Grill is on Second Avenue at Marion Street, in the Marion Building, which dates to 1903. Its steaks are custom dry-aged and seared over mesquite charcoal, and the beef comes from three sources at once — USDA Prime from Double R Ranch, American wagyu from Snake River Farms and Japanese A5. El Gaucho is up in Belltown at 2200 Western Avenue, in the former Union Stables at the corner of Blanchard, working 28-day dry-aged Niman Ranch Prime Certified Angus Beef, according to the restaurant's own menu, with a chateaubriand and a bone-in rib eye on the list.

The Capital Grille holds Fourth Avenue and Ruth's Chris holds Pine Street, the city's two national fine-dining outposts. Fogo de Chão is on University Street, where gaucho chefs fire-roast, butcher and serve at the table around a market table set in front of the grill. Buenos Aires Grill is the Argentine room on Virginia Street.

The Butcher's Table is the newest shape of the group, on Westlake Avenue in South Lake Union: a modern steakhouse built on Mishima Reserve American wagyu, with a butcher's case at the front stocked with the same beef and house-smoked meats.

sections.heading: Capitol Hill and the lakes
sections.body:
Three rooms east of downtown, two of them on the water.

Bateau is on East Union Street on Capitol Hill and is the whole-animal steak room on this page: beef is the programme rather than one section of the menu. Daniel's Broiler keeps two rooms inside the city, one on Fairview Place North at the south end of Lake Union and one on Lake Washington Boulevard in Leschi, both of them turned to the water. The group also runs a downtown Seattle room and one in Bellevue across the lake; Bellevue is outside this page, which measures inside the city limits first.

sections.heading: Ballard, Wallingford and the north end
sections.body:
Five rooms strung across the neighborhoods north of the ship canal, and not one of them is a chophouse in the downtown sense.

Asadero Prime is on Leary Avenue Northwest in Ballard, a Mexican steakhouse cooking USDA Prime and American wagyu over mesquite in Spanish-made Josper charcoal ovens that grill and roast in a single unit. Kokkaku is on North 45th Street in Wallingford, a Japanese-inspired meat house doing whole-beast butchery on a small nightly menu.

The Shambles is at 7777 15th Avenue Northeast, a 21-and-over room with old English pub bones, cutting its steaks in house and running house-made sausages and foraged mushrooms beside them. The Wedgwood Broiler is a few blocks east on 35th Avenue Northeast, selling its steaks by the ounce and putting prime rib on Wednesdays, Fridays, Saturdays and Sundays until it runs out. FlintCreek Cattle Co. is west of them on Greenwood Avenue North, buying from small-scale farms raising pastured, grass-fed animals, and putting an aged tomahawk on the menu.

sections.heading: West Seattle
sections.body:
One room across the bridge.

JaK's Grill is on Southwest Alaska Street in the Alaska Junction, a neighborhood steakhouse rather than a formal one. The group runs a second restaurant in Issaquah, which is outside the city and outside this page.

faq.question: Why is this a Seattle page rather than a Puget Sound one?
faq.answer: Because the count is inside the city. All sixteen rooms here are within the Seattle limits, concentrated downtown and in Belltown with the north-end neighborhoods behind them, so the page did not need to reach out to the suburbs. That is the exact inverse of this site's Korean barbecue survey, where Seattle's grills sat in four suburban corridors up to forty miles out and the page had to become a regional one to describe them honestly. Bellevue's steakhouse is real and is not needed here.

faq.question: What makes a room a steakhouse on this page?
faq.answer: Steak has to be the menu's center of gravity, plus the beef-centric genres — churrascaria, Argentine parrilla, Japanese wagyu counter, Korean-style beef room. In Seattle that rule does real work at the north end, where Asadero is a Mexican steakhouse, Kokkaku is a Japanese meat house and FlintCreek is a grass-fed beef room. It also keeps casual national chains off the page entirely.

faq.question: Which rooms did this survey check and leave off?
faq.answer: Four. Spencer's for Steaks and Chops could not be placed inside the city limits. Red Cow's own web address now redirects to its restaurant group's home page rather than to a restaurant, so it could not be confirmed as trading. BOCA at Queen City Grill could not be confirmed either. The Grill From Ipanema turns out to be a Washington DC churrascaria with no Seattle room. A room whose status cannot be verified is left off rather than published with a hedge.

faq.question: How many Daniel's Broiler rooms are on this page?
faq.answer: Two: Lake Union and Leschi. The group also runs a downtown Seattle room, mentioned above, and a Bellevue room across Lake Washington. Bellevue is a separate city and falls outside the scope this page set for itself.

faq.question: Why does JaK's Grill appear only once?
faq.answer: Because it has one room inside the city. The operator runs two restaurants, West Seattle and Issaquah, and Issaquah is twenty miles east on the far side of Lake Sammamish. Only the West Seattle room at 4209 Southwest Alaska Street is published here.

photos.title: The Marion Building on Second Avenue, Seattle
photos.description: A three-story grey stone and brick building on a downtown corner, MARION BUILDING carved into the stone above a columned entrance and MARION set into the parapet above that. Green awnings lettered MG run along the sidewalk and a green canopy reading Metropolitan Grill stands over the door; taller towers rise behind, and a woman in a red coat waits at the crossing on the left.
photos.author: Joe Mabel

places.name: Metropolitan Grill
places.summary: The Metropolitan Grill occupies the Marion Building at Second Avenue and Marion Street downtown, a building that dates to 1903. Steaks are custom dry-aged and seared over mesquite charcoal, and the beef runs from USDA Prime out of Double R Ranch to American wagyu from Snake River Farms and Japanese A5.

places.name: El Gaucho
places.summary: El Gaucho's Seattle room is in the old Union Stables building at Western Avenue and Blanchard Street in Belltown. The house serves 28-day dry-aged Niman Ranch Prime Certified Angus Beef, according to the restaurant's own menu, with a chateaubriand, a bone-in rib eye and filet mignon on the list.

places.name: The Butcher's Table
places.summary: The Butcher's Table is a modern steakhouse on Westlake Avenue in South Lake Union built on Mishima Reserve American wagyu beef. A butcher's case at the front is stocked with the same wagyu, house-smoked meats and other cuts off the menu.

places.name: The Capital Grille
places.summary: The Capital Grille's Seattle dining room is on Fourth Avenue downtown. Dry-aged steaks are what the house is built on.

places.name: Ruth's Chris Steak House
places.summary: Ruth's Chris keeps its Seattle room on Pine Street downtown, the city's outpost of the national chophouse chain.

places.name: Fogo de Chão
places.summary: Fogo de Chão's Seattle churrascaria is on University Street downtown, where gaucho chefs fire-roast, butcher and serve the beef tableside. The dining room is built around a market table anchored in front of the grill, with dry-aged meat lockers along the room.

places.name: Bateau
places.summary: Bateau is a whole-animal steak room on East Union Street on Capitol Hill. Beef is the program rather than one section of the menu, which is what puts it on this page.

places.name: The Shambles
places.summary: The Shambles calls itself a laid-back steak joint, and it is a 21-and-over room with old English pub bones. The steaks are cut in house, and house-made sausages and seasonal dishes from foraged mushrooms up run beside them.
places.history: The room opened in 2018 and was bought by its current owners in late 2022, according to the restaurant's own account.

places.name: Buenos Aires Grill
places.summary: Buenos Aires Grill is an Argentine parrilla on Virginia Street at the downtown edge of Belltown, where grilled beef is the center of the menu.

places.name: Asadero Prime
places.summary: Asadero Prime is a Mexican steakhouse on Leary Avenue Northwest in Ballard, serving USDA Prime and American wagyu cooked over mesquite. The kitchen works Spanish-made Josper charcoal ovens, which grill and oven-roast in a single unit.

places.name: Kokkaku
places.summary: Kokkaku is a Japanese-inspired meat house on North 45th Street in Wallingford, built on whole-beast butchery and local sourcing. Beef is the center of a small nightly menu served five evenings a week.

places.name: Daniel's Broiler, Lake Union
places.summary: Daniel's Broiler's Lake Union room stands on Fairview Place North at the south end of the lake, with the water on one side and the Prime 809 lounge upstairs. Steaks off the broiler are the menu.

places.name: Daniel's Broiler, Leschi
places.summary: Daniel's Broiler's Leschi room sits on Lake Washington Boulevard at the waterfront, the eastern end of the group's three-room run through the city. Steaks off the broiler are the menu, with a private loft above the dining room.

places.name: JaK's Grill
places.summary: JaK's Grill is a neighborhood steakhouse in the West Seattle junction on Southwest Alaska Street, working classic steakhouse cuts without the formality. It has been a West Seattle room since 1996, according to the restaurant's own description.

places.name: Wedgwood Broiler
places.summary: The Wedgwood Broiler is a neighborhood restaurant and cocktail lounge on 35th Avenue Northeast selling its steaks by the ounce. Prime rib runs Wednesday, Friday, Saturday and Sunday until it is gone, with filet mignon, New York steaks and a house London broil on the list beside it.
places.history: The room has carried the same broiler menu since 1965, according to the restaurant's own masthead.

places.name: FlintCreek Cattle Co.
places.summary: FlintCreek Cattle Co. is on Greenwood Avenue North in Phinney Ridge, buying premium meats from small-scale farms and ranches raising pastured, grass-fed animals without added hormones or antibiotics. An aged tomahawk and a twelve-ounce prime steak anchor the menu.

entries.name: Metropolitan Grill
entries.note: Second Avenue at Marion. Three grades of beef on one list, and the mesquite char is the house signature.

entries.name: El Gaucho
entries.note: 2200 Western Avenue, Belltown. The old Union Stables building; ask for the chateaubriand if there are two of you.

entries.name: The Butcher's Table
entries.note: Westlake Avenue, South Lake Union. Buy wagyu at the case on the way out.

entries.name: The Capital Grille
entries.note: Fourth Avenue downtown. The chain outpost that sits closest to the office towers.

entries.name: Ruth's Chris Steak House
entries.note: Pine Street, downtown. A short walk up from the retail core.

entries.name: Fogo de Chão
entries.note: University Street. The one churrascaria downtown, with the market table in front of the grill.

entries.name: Bateau
entries.note: East Union Street, Capitol Hill. Whole-animal beef, which is the sharpest version of this page's rule.

entries.name: The Shambles
entries.note: 15th Avenue Northeast. Steaks cut in house, and the bar is where the room actually happens.

entries.name: Buenos Aires Grill
entries.note: Virginia Street. The Argentine grill on the page, at the downtown end of Belltown.

entries.name: Asadero Prime
entries.note: Leary Avenue Northwest, Ballard. Josper ovens and mesquite; a Mexican steakhouse rather than a chophouse.

entries.name: Kokkaku
entries.note: North 45th Street, Wallingford. Whole-beast butchery on a small menu, Wednesday through Sunday only.

entries.name: Daniel's Broiler, Lake Union
entries.note: Fairview Place North, on the lake. The Prime 809 lounge upstairs is the room with the view.

entries.name: Daniel's Broiler, Leschi
entries.note: Lake Washington Boulevard. The quietest of the group's rooms and the one on the eastern shore.

entries.name: JaK's Grill
entries.note: Southwest Alaska Street, the West Seattle junction. The one room on this page across the bridge.

entries.name: Wedgwood Broiler
entries.note: 35th Avenue Northeast. Steaks sold by the ounce, and prime rib four days a week while it lasts.

entries.name: FlintCreek Cattle Co.
entries.note: Greenwood Avenue North. Small farms, grass-fed animals, and an aged tomahawk at the top of the list.
